I: Contact dermatitis/exacerbation - Could be worsening eczema triggered by irritants or allergens causing inflammation
Secondary bacterial infection - Eczema commonly complicated by impetigo or secondary infection leading to redness and soreness
D: Eczema flare due to skin barrier dysfunction and dryness - Worsening of chronic atopic dermatitis possibly due to environmental or internal triggers
Nutritional deficiency (e.g., essential fatty acid deficiency) - Less likely but can present with dry, itchy skin
I2: Steroid resistance or inappropriate use - Using hydrocortisone cream not strong enough for severe flare
C: Atopic dermatitis (congenital component) - Patient history of eczema from past supports this
A: Atopic/allergic dermatitis - Underlying allergic pathophysiology contributes to eczema
Other allergic dermatitis causes (e.g., environmental allergens)
E: Asthma and atopic dermatitis as part of an atopic triad indicating systemic atopic predisposition
Thyroid disease (family history) - unlikely cause here but metabolic/endocrine causes of skin changes possible
